comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citi disclose total Commercial Real Estate (CRE) exposure for fiscal year 2024, but the magnitude and composition differ significantly. JPM reports a total Real Estate exposure of $207.1 billion, with specific mention of downgrades in Multifamily and Office segments driving criticized exposure increases. In contrast, Citi reports a much smaller total CRE exposure of $65 billion, explicitly breaking out $6 billion of office building exposure, and notes that the majority of its exposure (approximately $56 billion) is related to corporate clients rather than direct CRE property lending.

sentences.text: Real Estate exposure was $207.1 billion as of December 31, 2024.
Criticized exposure increased by $3.2 billion from $9.2 billion at December 31, 2023 to $12.4 billion at December 31, 2024, predominantly driven by downgrades, primarily in Multifamily and Office.

As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Citi's total credit exposure to commercial real estate (CRE) was $65 billion and $66 billion, including $6 billion and $8 billion of exposure related to office buildings, respectively.
This total CRE exposure consisted of approximately $56 billion and $55 billion, respectively, related to corporate clients, included in the real estate category in the tables above and below.

comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Real Estate Lending Exposure and Amounts
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, lending against commercial real estate properties totaled $10.7 billion and $9.4 billion, respectively, representing 4.4% and 4.5% of total exposure in the Institutional Securities segment.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Morgan Stanley disclose lending exposure specifically to commercial real estate (CRE) properties, but Morgan Stanley's exposure is substantially lower in absolute terms. JPM's total Real Estate exposure is $207.1 billion, while Morgan Stanley reports only $10.7 billion in lending against CRE properties within its Institutional Securities segment. Furthermore, Morgan Stanley highlights that these loans are generally syndicated or securitized to reduce ongoing exposure, a risk mitigation detail not present in JPM's summary of the $207.1 billion exposure.

sentences.text: Real Estate exposure was $207.1 billion as of December 31, 2024.

As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, our lending against commercial real estate ("CRE") properties within the Institutional Securities business segment totaled $10.7 billion and $9.4 billion, respectively.
In many cases, loans are subsequently syndicated or securitized on a full or partial basis, reducing our ongoing exposure.
